subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Dark Energy: The Accelerating Universe
description: A quick, practical guide to Dark Energy: The Accelerating Universe.

hook.text: The universe isn't just expanding—it's speeding up. Something is pushing space apart, and nobody knows what.

buildup.text: In 1998, two teams studying distant supernovae expected to find the expansion slowing. They found the opposite.

discovery.text: The results showed expansion is accelerating. The unknown cause was named dark energy—it makes up 68% of the universe.

twist.text: Einstein's discarded cosmological constant fits the data perfectly. His 'biggest blunder' might have been correct all along.

climax.text: Perlmutter, Schmidt, and Riess won the 2011 Nobel Prize. Dark energy remains the biggest mystery in physics.

punchline.text: Sixty-eight percent of the universe. Completely mysterious. Pushing everything apart.

quiz.question: What was surprising about the 1998 supernova observations?
options: The universe's expansion is accelerating rather than slowing down
Supernovae were brighter than expected in distant galaxies
Dark matter was found to be repelling galaxies

details.summary: Dark energy is a mysterious force driving the universe's expansion to accelerate — discovered in 1998 through observations of distant Type Ia supernovae. It constitutes about 68% of the universe's total energy content. Its nature is completely unknown, making it the biggest mystery in physics.
details.whyItMatters: Dark energy determines the universe's ultimate fate. If it remains constant, the universe expands forever and grows cold. If it strengthens, a 'Big Rip' could tear apart galaxies, stars, and atoms.
takeaways: Dark energy drives the accelerating expansion of the universe
It makes up about 68% of the universe's energy content
Its nature is completely unknown — physics' biggest mystery

faq.question: Is dark energy the same as Einstein's cosmological constant?
faq.answer: Possibly. Einstein introduced the cosmological constant as a 'fudge factor' to keep the universe static, then abandoned it when expansion was discovered. The simplest explanation for dark energy is a constant energy density of empty space — equivalent to Einstein's constant.

faq.question: When did dark energy start dominating the universe?
faq.answer: About 5 billion years ago. Before that, matter's gravity slowed expansion. As the universe expanded and matter diluted, dark energy's constant density became dominant, tipping the balance from deceleration to acceleration. We live in the era of dark energy dominance.
